blocks.text: Imagine running a small shop in Lagos and wanting to know if your business is profitable. The Profit and Loss Account is your go-to tool for this!

blocks.markdown: The Profit and Loss Account is a financial statement that shows the revenues and expenses of a business over a specific period, typically a year. It helps determine the net profit or loss by subtracting operating expenses from the gross profit.

blocks.title: Definition: Gross Profit
blocks.text: Gross profit is the difference between sales revenue and the cost of goods sold (COGS).

blocks.markdown: To prepare a Profit and Loss Account, start with the gross profit calculated from the trading account. Then, deduct operating expenses such as rent, salaries, and utilities to arrive at the net profit.

blocks.title: Preparing a Profit and Loss Account
blocks.prompt: Given the following information, prepare a Profit and Loss Account: Sales = ₦500,000, COGS = ₦300,000, Rent = ₦50,000, Salaries = ₦70,000.

steps.text: Calculate Net Profit: Gross Profit - Operating Expenses = ₦200,000 - ₦120,000.

blocks.markdown: It's crucial to distinguish between capital and revenue expenditures. Capital expenditures are for acquiring or upgrading physical assets, while revenue expenditures are for the day-to-day running of the business.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember, an omitted accrual will understate expenses and overstate net profit, which can mislead stakeholders.

points: The Profit and Loss Account helps determine the net profit by deducting operating expenses from gross profit.
Distinguishing between capital and revenue expenditures is essential for accurate financial reporting.
